provenance: patch 9: toolchain-diff — mask-load vs enable-test order plus test spelling: CL loads the dlg mask (66 8b 08) FIRST, then spells the enable test in a register (mov dl,[esp+8] 8a 54 24 08 + test dl,dl 84 d2 + je); FA tests the stack arg in place first (cmp byte ptr [esp+8],0 = 80 7c 24 08 00) and interleaves the mask load between the test and the je. 11→10 byte span rewrite, no relocs inside.

patch 23: toolchain-diff — je rel8 recompute (0x2e→0x30): the enable-arm je (test ch,0x80) aims at the shared ret; the or cx,0x8000 expansion (patch 36) grows the span +2, pushing the ret 2 B downstream (0x48), so FA's rel8 is 2 larger than CL's.
patch 30: toolchain-diff — jmp rel8 recompute (0x08→0x0a): same +2 cause (patch 36 lies between CL's jmp and its store target), target = the 16-bit mask store at FA 0x29.
patch 35: toolchain-diff — jne rel8 recompute (0x22→0x24): same +2 cause, target = the shared ret 0x48.

patch 36: toolchain-diff — 16-bit mask OR spelling: CL materializes or ch,0x80 (80 cd 80, 3 B) on the high byte of the cx-mask; FA emits the operand-size-prefixed whole-word form or cx,0x8000 (66 81 c9 00 80, 5 B). Same-site 3→5 rewrite (no relocs inside); downstream rel8s recomputed by patches 23/30/35.

patch 11: toolchain-diff — je rel8 recompute (0x11→0x23): CL inlines the proto==1 arm (mov ax,2) before the call, so its je aims 0x11 ahead at 0x1d; FA moves the arm past the ret (patch 47) and deletes CL's copies (patch 27), so the je aims at the tail block 0x2f — rel8 rebuilt.
patch 21: toolchain-diff — jle rel8 recompute (0x0d→0x1f): same cause — the proto 4/5 arm (mov ax,1) is FA's tail block at 0x35 instead of CL's inline copy at 0x23.

patch 45: toolchain-diff — epilogue split: CL cleans the two pushed args as one add esp,8 (83 c4 08); FA pops them in two halves (add esp,4 … add esp,4) with a dead (void-returned) test/setne/mov al,cl block wedged between (85 c0 / 0f 95 c1 / 8a c1) — FA's compiler tested the call result although the function's return value is discarded. 3→13 byte span rewrite; no relocs inside (the call's REL32 sits before the span and shifts cleanly to FA's 0x1d site).

patch 27: toolchain-diff — deletes CL's 12 bytes of forward-jmp + inlined switch arms (eb 0a; mov ax,2; eb 04; mov ax,1) before the call; FA's default arm falls straight into the push (no jmp), and FA's arm copies live past the ret (patch 47).

patch 47: toolchain-diff — inserts FA's two tail-arm blocks after the ret (at 0x2f): mov ax,0x0002 / jmp −0x1a and mov ax,0x0001 / jmp −0x20 (66 b8 02 00 eb e6, 66 b8 01 00 eb e0) — both backward jmps rejoin the push at 0x1b. CL has no spelling that moves switch arms after the ret.

patch 27: toolchain-diff — 16-bit sub encoding inside inline asm: for `sub ax,0x3f` MASM always spells the imm16 form (66 2d 3f 00, 4 B); FA uses the o16 imm8 form (66 83 e8 3f = sub ax,imm8 0x3f, 4 B). Same-length 4-B span rewrite to FA's encoding; no relocs inside.

patch 10: toolchain-diff — je rel8 recompute (0x12→0x14): FA's align-loop je aims at the word-scan loop entry (the 8b 01 reload of *[str]); the 2-byte growth of FA's own mid-function pad (patch 27) sits between, so FA's rel8 is 2 larger (0x14 vs CL 0x12).

patch 17: toolchain-diff — je rel8 recompute (0x3e→0x40): FA's fast-path je (after the 0x7efefeff magic check) aims at the slow byte-loop; the same mid-function pad sits between, so its rel8 is 2 larger (0x40 vs CL 0x3e).

patch 27: toolchain-diff — mid-function pad: FA pads between the align-loop fallthrough and the word-scan loop with the 5-byte add eax,0 (05 00000000, census VOCAB filler); CL spells the dead add as the redundant 3-byte 83 c0 00 there. 3→5 byte same-site rewrite (all downstream rel8s recomputed by patches 10/17).

patch 0: toolchain-diff — cmp-before-pushes prologue: FA tests the lock counter in memory BEFORE the esi/edi saves (cmp dword ptr [__nstream+0x4],0 — 83 3d, 7 B); CL pushes esi and a1-loads the counter first, then push edi and test eax,eax. First byte of the modrm pair.

patch 1: toolchain-diff — companion modrm of the same FA cmp (3d = [disp32],imm8 form); the disp32 itself is CL's own DIR32 reloc at 0x2 (already symbol-anchored, zero content) so only the opcode bytes change — the __nstream+0x4 VA (0x00589d84) lands exactly like FA's.

patch 6: toolchain-diff — prologue reg-plan swap completion: the in-place cmp form is 1 B shorter than CL's a1-load+test sequence, so FA's push esi/push edi sits at 0x07-0x08 while CL has push edi at 0x06 and test eax at 0x07-0x08; this 3-B span spells FA's bytes (00 = the cmp imm8, then 56 57).
patch 13: toolchain-diff — flag/result register swap (CL: flag=esi, result=edi; FA: flag=edi, result=esi — the register plan CL 4.2 always picks for this decl order). mov esi,1 → mov edi,1 (be→bf).
patch 29: toolchain-diff — register swap: CL xor esi,esi (33 f6) → FA xor edi,edi (33 ff) in the no-lock arm that bumps the __nstream counter.
patch 54: toolchain-diff — register swap: CL mov edi,eax (8b f8) for the wctomb_lk return copy → FA mov esi,eax (8b f0).
patch 56: toolchain-diff — register swap companion: CL test esi,esi on the flag → FA test edi,edi (85 f6 → 85 ff) guarding unlock vs counter-decrement.
patch 71: toolchain-diff — register swap: CL mov eax,edi (8b c7) return copy → FA mov eax,esi (8b c6), unlock arm.
patch 76: toolchain-diff — register swap: CL mov eax,edi (8b c7) return copy in the decrement arm → FA mov eax,esi (8b c6).

patch 77: toolchain-diff — tail scheduling: CL execs the counter decrement BEFORE the register pops (dec [gctr2]; pop edi; pop esi; ret); FA pops the frame regs first, then decs [__nstream+0x8], then rets. 9-B span reordered (5f 5e … ff 0d …); the DIR32 newsite 4 B into the span re-anchors the counter VA (0x00589d88) that CL's dropped reloc used to carry.
